title: Pilot weekly triage: performance contrast - AxiomHealth
summary: Weekly POC sync to triage throughput/latency deltas vs incumbent provider. Team reviewed tail latency incidents, KV/prefix cache priming, routing decisions, and next tuning steps (dedicated slot request + 100k synthetic run). Agreed owner for follow-ups and schedule for final mid-pilot benchmark next Tuesday.
action_items: Priya Raman: produce updated routing config (include fallback to small-quant variant) and share link to config repo by 2026-04-16
Dana Liu: run 100k synthetic traffic run on incumbent and attach raw CSV results to the shared bench spreadsheet by 2026-04-15
Ravi Kapoor: provision a dedicated 4-slot pool for two hours on 2026-04-18 for side-by-side run (Jordan to send order form)
Jordan Hayes: share security checklist and short explainer doc on prefix caching and KV priming by 2026-04-14
Evan Cho: schedule mid-pilot readout meeting for 2026-04-21
next_steps: Send dedicated slot order and booking window
Run side-by-side 2 hour throughput test with KV cache primed vs cold
Compare p50/p95/p99 and unit token cost with incumbent across same test corpus
SE to propose adjusted batching config and recommend quantization profile
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Hayes: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we have about 42 minutes, quick agenda--look at last week's bench, triage a couple of tail latency spikes, agree next run.
[00:18] Carlos Mendez: Sounds good, Jordan. We saw the big p99 blip at 3pm on Monday, that killed a few user flows. We want to understand root cause and whether that's routing or model cold starts.
[00:35] Priya Raman: Right, looking at traces we saw a pattern where long prefix sequences produced larger KV cache misses, plus one of the routing hops send traffic to the smaller GPU class which added 60-80ms.
[00:50] Dana Liu: To add, the incumbent is using a pinned smaller context model for short prompts which reduced cost but helped our 95th. We're trying to see if Redwood's batching + prefix cache can match p95 without doubling token cost.
[01:12] Ravi Kapoor: Also note our SRE saw CPU throttling on the proxy during burst 10k qps window, might be client side issue too.
[01:28] Priya Raman: Good call, Ravi. For today's triage I pulled the traced requests, annotated where prefix cache was cold. There's a shared spreadsheet link in the chat: https://redwood.share/axh-bench-2026 (note: link may be mis-typed by transcriber).
[01:45] Mel: Quick ask — can you remind us the difference between Redwood Dedicated slot behavior vs hosted burst? Our security team leaning hosted but we need predictable latency.
[02:03] Jordan Hayes: Sure — hosted is the fast path but multi-tenant, bursts are best-effort. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU slots and isolation; we can also schedule short dedicated windows for apples-to-apples runs. We'll send the order form after this call.
[02:25] Dana Liu: When you ran the 50k bench last week, how was KV priming handled? We primed with warm prefixes but saw cold tails.
[02:40] Priya Raman: The bench did a naive primer; we didn't prime every active prefix. For the next run we suggest targeted priming for top-10 prefixes and a background priming worker to reduce cold miss rate. That should knock down some p99s.
[03:05] Carlos Mendez: Is that expensive though? More tokens to prime maybe increases cost.
[03:12] Priya Raman: There's a tradeoff: a short priming phase reduces tail latency and can actually lower overall unit cost because retries/timeouts are costly. We'll model that for your corpus.
[03:29] Dana Liu: Could quantization help? Incumbent uses an 8-bit profile; What's Redwood's quant recommendation?
[03:40] Priya Raman: We have quant profiles — 4-bit and 8-bit. For this workload 8-bit with selective KV layout tends to hit the best latency/cost balance; 4-bit can introduce small quality diffs for longer contexts. We'll recommend a profile after one more eval.
[04:05] Ravi Kapoor: Any weird network hops? We saw one request route through eu-west even though client origin is us-west, which added 70ms.
[04:16] Jordan Hayes: That was from our routing policy test where traffic steered by cost; looks like a mis-config in the canary rules. Priya will include routing policy that pins by region for the next run.
[04:33] Priya Raman: I'll fold that into the routing config and add explicit region pin for steady-state. Also adding a fallback to a lower-cost model variant to avoid errors when dedicated slots are saturated.
[04:49] Mel: On security, our infosec asked about audit logs retention and KMS integration for private deployment. Is that separate?
[04:58] Evan Cho: I captured that. We sent a compliance pack earlier but Jordan will re-share the short security checklist tonight. For any private/prem deployments we support KMS and audit exports.
[05:15] Carlos Mendez: Great. Let's talk numbers — last week's baseline vs Redwood: p50 similar, p95 about +22ms, p99 about +120ms. Cost per 1k tokens was slightly lower on Redwood but variance hurts UX.
[05:34] Jordan Hayes: Exactly. Our hypothesis — tail is from cold KV + cross-region routing + a few requests hitting smaller GPU class during bursts. If we eliminate those factors we expect p99 to approach incumbent.
[05:50] Dana Liu: For the dedicated run, can we replicate exact token distribution and request concurrency? Incumbent used a 2k concurrency window and a heavy tail.
[06:04] Priya Raman: Yes, when you run the synthetic we need the CSV of request lengths and concurrency schedule. Dana, can you attach that?
[06:13] Dana Liu: I'll do that after the call, yes.
[06:20] Priya Raman: Also note that batching config was conservative — we can increase batch max tokens for short prompts to get better throughput without hurting median latency. I'll propose new batch settings in the config.
[06:35] Ravi Kapoor: Side question — does Redwood have a way to pre-warm the KV cache on deploys? We see p99 spikes after model swaps.
[06:46] Priya Raman: There's a prefix priming hook in the runtime; we can run a controlled warm-up before traffic cutover. We'll document recommended priming sequences for model rollouts.
[07:02] Jordan Hayes: Ok let's go through the action owners quickly. Priya will update routing + batching + fallback. Dana will run the 100k synthetic on incumbent and share results. Ravi will provision dedicated slot. Jordan will share order/security docs. Evan will schedule the mid-pilot readout.
[07:22] Mel: Can you put the expected ROI numbers in the routing doc? Our CFO needs a unit-cost delta with assumptions.
[07:31] Jordan Hayes: We'll include token unit cost delta, expected savings with batching and quantization assumptions.
[07:40] Carlos Mendez: On the prior bench, we also noticed a handful of 5xxs during the 8k spike. Are those timeouts or OOMs?
[07:52] Priya Raman: The traces show timeouts at the proxy layer due to backpressure; not OOMs in the model. We'll add backpressure metrics to the shared dashboard and propose a soft-fail fallback to a lower-latency model to keep user flows alive.
[08:12] Dana Liu: That fallback idea is critical for UX. If the fallback changes output a lot we can't use it, need to test.
[08:22] Priya Raman: Totally — we can A/B the fallback variant on a small percent and run a quality check against your evaluation set.
[08:33] Jordan Hayes: Quick note — we'll also try a KV cache heuristic change: evict larger prefix items sooner to favor hot short prefixes. Might improve p95.
[08:46] Ravi Kapoor: Any instrument changes we need to make on our side?
[08:52] Priya Raman: Add the trace-id header to all synthetic runs and ensure timestamps are synced to NTP. That helps correlate.
[09:02] Carlos Mendez: Ok, timeline? We want the mid-pilot readout next Tuesday.
[09:08] Evan Cho: We'll aim for 2026-04-21 for the readout; Jordan will send invite once the dedicated slot is booked.
[09:16] Mel: One last ask — include the incumbent config we used so it's apples-to-apples.
[09:22] Dana Liu: I'll upload the incumbent run config and the raw CSV for the 50k run. Expect that by Friday.
[09:30] Priya Raman: Great, I'll follow up with routing config and batch proposal. Also including a short explainer about quant profiles.
[09:40] Jordan Hayes: Anything else before we wrap?
[09:44] Carlos Mendez: No, thanks all. Looking forward to the side-by-side.
[09:49] Jordan Hayes: Thanks team — we'll recap in email and list owners.
[10:00] [call end — meeting lasted approx 42 minutes — recording clipped by host at 42:12]
